problem.title_as_question: Why do amateur players brush the ball differently from pros when trying to hit topspin?
problem.definition: Players often try to create topspin by purely brushing or pulling up across the back of the ball without driving through, resulting in floaty rotation with no penetration or control.

symptoms.description: The ball has spin and rotation but lacks driving power and penetration, producing a weak floaty ball.
The trunk fails to connect to the swing and cannot transfer energy into the hand strike.
The player pulls the arm straight upward with level shoulders instead of driving forward on a shallow diagonal.

causes.statement: The player attempts to generate topspin by purely rolling or brushing upward without driving the racket head forward through the ball.
The player fails to set the correct lateral spacing or depth relative to the power slot, causing the hand to fight the swing rather than rolling naturally.
The player leans back to lift the ball instead of leaning in and lowering the body stance inside the court.
The player conceptualizes the swing path as a symmetrical C shape or dive-bombs steep down-and-up rather than a forward-driving Nike swoosh diagonal.
The player keeps the shoulders level, leaving upward arm pulling as the only way to impart spin.

angles.summary: The coach compares the proper topspin swing shape to the Nike swoosh rather than a circular C loop, emphasizing a shallow forward diagonal.
The coach demonstrates pure rolling with no hit versus driving through with a below-horizontal incidence angle.
A slight shoulder slant and low body stance allow the racket to approach on a shallow downward angle while driving forward and up through contact.
Players wrongly assume topspin requires pulling up aggressively with the hand or jumping backwards to lift the ball.

solutions.summary: Approach the ball with a racket incidence angle below horizontal and drive straight through the ball.
Lower your knees and hips as much as possible so the hand starts lower without altering comfortable swing mechanics.
Experiment with arm firing depth and lateral distance from the power slot until the hand naturally wants to roll through contact without fighting.
Ensure the hand gets closer to the level of the ball before forward acceleration to prevent dive-bombing down into contact.
Oscillate between focusing consciously on a cue (like hand height or incidence angle) and hitting with a blank mind until the movement becomes automatic.
Execute the adaptive response drill by alternating between running forward to hit flatter on short balls and hitting heavy topspin while balanced or backing up.
